_note: Qualitative scout notes (role / fit / risk). Live numbers (ranks, phase shares, values) are added automatically from the data so the notes stay correct after re-runs. Players without a note get an auto-generated profile.

Reeza Hendricks.fit: The most reliable chaser in the pool: most of his pressure balls come in second innings, and he is at his best in the tightest moments. Cover for the opening pair and a stabiliser at No.3.
Reeza Hendricks.risk: No IPL contract history, so his evidence comes from T20Is (opposition-adjusted).

Towhid Hridoy.fit: Beats expectation in most of his pressure innings, mostly in chases, and finishes strongly at the death, RR's weaker batting phase. A low-cost middle-order option.
Towhid Hridoy.risk: Bangladesh player: registered for 2027, but there is political risk after the January 2026 KKR episode. No IPL sample.

Mohammad Nabi.fit: A specialist for the last five overs when setting a total: the profile RR lacked at the death.
Mohammad Nabi.risk: Age 41; his off-spin rates below par under pressure; poor when chasing.

Daryl Mitchell.fit: Dominates spin in the middle overs, rotates the strike and clears the ropes; 435 ODI runs v India in 2026. Stability plus muscle around Ferreira.
Daryl Mitchell.risk: Value buy: unsold on a Rs 2 cr base in 2026.

Sikandar Raza.fit: Rated in both our batting and bowling top 10s: a middle-overs chaser with the bat and a middle-overs control spinner with the ball. One overseas slot covers two needs at a low price.

Kyle Mayers.fit: A powerplay pressure batter who is strong against pace.
Kyle Mayers.risk: RR's powerplay batting is already the league's best under pressure, so this is depth, not need.

Harry Brook.fit: Elite in normal play and still above par under pressure. An anchor-aggressor for the middle order.
Harry Brook.risk: Must register (two-season ban lapsed; has said he may return). Likely Rs 4-8 cr.

George Dockrell.fit: Better under pressure than in normal play, with most of his pressure balls at the death. A near-base-price finishing option.
George Dockrell.risk: No IPL exposure; mostly bilateral T20I evidence.

Roston Chase.fit: Makes both lists: economical middle-overs off-spin and a useful lower-middle-order bat.

Jonny Bairstow.risk: Age 37; fewer recent pressure innings than the list's evidence bar.

Mujeeb Ur Rahman.fit: The best available pressure bowler in our ratings. Most of his pressure overs come defending totals, and he controls the powerplay and middle overs. Young (25).
Mujeeb Ur Rahman.risk: Limited IPL time since 2021; price could rise if teams see the same numbers.

Mustafizur Rahman.fit: The death specialist RR need: over half of his pressure overs come at the death, the phase where RR rank near the bottom under pressure. IPL-proven over 8 seasons.
Mustafizur Rahman.risk: Political risk: KKR had to release him in January 2026. Bid with a fallback ready (Mark Adair, Ngarava or Taskin; Ferguson or Pathirana if released).

Maheesh Theekshana.fit: A large proven sample across all three phases. Played for RR in 2025.
Maheesh Theekshana.risk: Unsold in 2026 on a Rs 2 cr base, so expect value.

Mark Adair.fit: A death-and-powerplay seamer who beats expectation under pressure: a low-cost death-bowling fallback.

Richard Ngarava.fit: Above-par powerplay and death bowling under pressure. A low-cost left-arm angle.

FazalHaq Farooqi.risk: His IPL pressure sample is below par.

Taskin Ahmed.fit: Above-par pace in the powerplay and at the death. A death-bowling fallback.
Taskin Ahmed.risk: Bangladesh political-risk flag; no IPL history.

Mohit Sharma.fit: The best Indian option in the auction pool by our ratings: a death-overs cutter specialist and IPL veteran who fills an Indian slot cheaply.

Lockie Ferguson.fit: The best pressure bowler on the release list: pace in the powerplay, middle and death.
Lockie Ferguson.risk: Big purses (LSG, KKR, SRH, DC) will chase him - set a ceiling.

Matheesha Pathirana.fit: Slingy death specialist and one of the best pressure bowlers on the release list.
Matheesha Pathirana.risk: Will be the most contested bowler - set a ceiling.

Cameron Green.fit: Average under pressure in our ratings.
Cameron Green.risk: Rs 25.2 cr. If released, a KKR buy-back is likely and beyond RR's purse.

Blessing Muzarabani.fit: Above-par pressure seamer, released by KKR: a value overseas pace option.

M Shahrukh Khan.fit: Pure muscle for overs 15-20 or the impact-batter role.

Kamindu Mendis.fit: Overseas middle-order stability who also bowls spin with either arm.

Tushar Deshpande.fit: IPL-proven Indian quick who knows RR; bowls the tough overs at the death.
Tushar Deshpande.risk: Price should be sensible after release.

Wanindu Hasaranga.role: Leg-spin, middle overs - the trusted spinner
Wanindu Hasaranga.fit: Proven IPL wrist-spinner and ex-RR: takes wickets through the middle overs and partners the spin attack.
Wanindu Hasaranga.risk: Will attract bids from teams with big purses.

Nitish Rana.fit: Takes the innings from over 12 to the finish: rotates against spin, clears the ropes at the death, and partners Ferreira. Ex-RR.
Nitish Rana.risk: DC, KKR and MI need Indian batters: max ₹5.5 cr.

Shimron Hetmyer.fit: Explosive left-handed finisher; available well below his previous fee.

Nehal Wadhera.fit: Left-handed middle-order batter who holds the innings together through overs 12-16 and then shifts gears at the death; an Indian, so no overseas slot used.
Nehal Wadhera.risk: DC, KKR, MI and PBKS need Indian batters: max ₹5 cr.

Rachin Ravindra.fit: Flexible batter who adds a spin option.

Ishant Sharma.fit: Veteran new-ball seamer; reliable powerplay overs and experience.

Avesh Khan.fit: Indian backup pace for Shami and Sandeep; ex-RR (2024).

Gerald Coetzee.fit: Genuine pace plus lower-order hitting: covers the injury-prone quicks and adds muscle at No.8.

Trent Boult.fit: Backup new-ball and death bowler behind Archer; ex-RR (2022-24) who knows Jaipur.

Mayank Markande.fit: Indian wrist-spin option that keeps an overseas slot free.

Rahul Tripathi.fit: Experienced Indian batter who can float in the order.

Ben Duckett.fit: Aggressive left-handed top-order batter who plays spin well.

Spencer Johnson.fit: Tall left-arm quick for the powerplay and death.

Karun Nair.fit: Experienced top-order cover for Jurel and Parag; plays spin well.

Mahipal Lomror.fit: Ex-RR finisher who knows Jaipur: muscle at No.6/7 and an extra left-hand option.

Prashant Veer.fit: Uncapped Indian hitter plus left-arm spin.

Matthew Breetzke.fit: Cover for Jurel and Parag at 3-4 who can also bat at No.5 or open; in strong 2026 ODI form (112 v Australia, Sep).

Mitchell Owen.fit: Clean striker for overs 12-20 who also bowls pace: the extra muscle the lower middle order needs.

Dunith Wellalage.fit: Young all-rounder who bats in the lower middle order and bowls left-arm spin: depth and a player to develop.

Deepak Chahar.fit: Powerplay wicket-taker who swings the new ball and bats at No.8-9; plays domestic cricket for Rajasthan (2026-27 SMAT captain).

Matt Henry.fit: In top international form (6/27 v India, 13 Nov 2026): hits the seam hard in the powerplay and covers Archer and Shami.
